meta.title: Record Now, Merge Later
meta.subtitle: Every worker writes its own lock-free chain; playback merges them with a heap keyed on a number you chose

views.label: Why there is no lock
views.note: Each worker thread owns its own chain of blocks. Two threads never touch the same bytes, so recording needs no synchronisation at all.

views.label: The number you choose is the order
views.note: Playback is a k-way merge of the chains, always taking the smallest key next. Pass the same key twice and the tie is not defined.

views.label: The merge is the barrier
views.note: Playback completes the producer jobs, then applies every recorded change on the main thread. One barrier instead of hundreds.

views.label: The handles were never fake
views.note: Recording a create allocates a real entity id on the spot. It simply has no chunk until playback puts it in one.

cards.title: Why recording needs no lock
items: There is one chain per worker thread, plus one for the main thread · EntityCommandBuffer.cs:288
A parallel writer picks its chain from the thread index alone · EntityCommandBufferParallelWriter.cs:82
Each chain is a linked list of blocks, four kibibytes by default · EntityCommandBuffer.cs:93
Commands are appended by bumping an offset inside the current block

cards.title: Playback is a k-way merge
items: Every non-empty chain becomes one entry in a priority queue · EntityCommandBufferPlayback.cs:303
Pop the smallest key, run that chain until it passes the next-smallest · line 306
Then push the chain back with its new head key and repeat · line 340
The heap orders strictly on the key, so the thread that recorded it is irrelevant

cards.title: The key is the whole contract
items: The documentation names the chunk index in the query as the value to pass · EntityCommandBufferParallelWriter.cs:87
That index is stable for a given world state, which is what makes playback repeatable
Main-thread commands are stamped with the largest possible integer · EntityCommandBuffer.cs:437
So anything you record outside a job is applied after everything recorded inside one

cards.title: The handles were never placeholders
items: Recording a create allocates real entity ids immediately · EntityCommandBuffer.cs:499
The parallel writer does exactly the same from inside a job · EntityCommandBufferParallelWriter.cs:156
The documentation says it plainly: valid at once, no chunk until playback · EntityCommandBuffer.cs:485
There is even a source comment worrying about the atomic contention this costs · line 153 of the parallel writer
